Shuka and Sarana, the Spies

Stories from the Ramayana

Shuka and Sarana, the Spies

They went to the enemy — and Rama let them go

In everyday English — Yuddha Kanda, sargas 20, 24–30

Stories by Eku

How to Read · · BEFORE WE BEGIN

Read it aloud. This story is made to be told. Read slowly, as if you were sitting among family at home.

This book is the story of spies. There is no great battle in it — only going in secret, being caught, and being set free. Where the spies slip in quietly, whisper; where Rama sets them free, let kindness into your voice.

The yellow boxes hold the characters speaking in their own words. Change your voice a little as you read them — Shuka frightened, Sugriva proud, Rama calm and steady, Sardula trembling.

(The purple cues) tell you where to pause, whisper, or raise your voice. They are for the reader — do not read them aloud.

The green box at the end of each part — Pause and think. Stop there. Ask the question. Let the listeners speak.

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 20 and 24–30 — Shuka and Sarana, the spies. Anything else you may want to know is given separately at the end, in Where This Story Comes From.

Who's Who · · WHO'S WHO

Ravana — king of Lanka, tall and splendid, dark-complexioned, black moustache, tall golden crown, royal robes. A single-headed royal form — as fixed in this series' Ravana book. He wants to know how strong Rama's army is.

Shuka — Ravana's minister and spy. Clever, loyal — first he goes to Sugriva as an envoy, then he enters the army as a spy.

Sarana — Ravana's minister and spy, Shuka's companion. He too takes a vanara's form and enters the army.

Sardula — Ravana's spy. He is the first to see Rama's army and return — and in the end he is sent again.

Rama — son of Dasharatha, tall and calm, warm dark-brown skin, wearing his upper cloth, bow in hand. He does not kill the captured spies — he sets them free.

Lakshmana — Rama's younger brother, a little lighter in complexion, bow in hand. He stands beside Rama.

Sugriva — king of the vanaras, warm brown fur, long tail, royal dress, plain gold crown. He answers Ravana through Shuka.

Vibhishana — Ravana's younger brother, now with Rama. He recognises the hidden spies.

Angada — son of Vali and Tara, a young vanara prince. He is the first to say — this is not an envoy, this is a spy.

1 · The First Spy — Sardula · · THE FIRST SPY — SARDULA

Rama's army was on the shore of the sea — and in Lanka, Ravana was worried. He did not know how big the army was, who was in it, or what Rama would do.

Ravana called his spy Sardula — “Go, look at the army — look from all sides — and come back and tell me.”

Sardula went — quietly, in hiding. He looked at the army from all sides — on the mountains, in the caves, on the shore of the sea, in the forests — there were vanaras everywhere.

Sardula grew afraid — and came swiftly back to Lanka. He said to Ravana — “Your Majesty, the army is so great it cannot be counted.”

Ravana heard this — and his heart was troubled. At once he thought — first, let Sugriva be talked out of it.

Ravana called Shuka — his cleverest minister.

Pause and think — Why did Ravana send a spy first? Is it necessary to know the enemy before a war? And why was Sardula afraid when he saw the army — is it natural to be afraid at the sight of a great army?

2 · Shuka Goes as Envoy · · SHUKA GOES AS ENVOY

Ravana said to Shuka — “Take the form of a bird — and go to Sugriva. Tell him — leave Rama, go back to Kishkindha. Do not give your life for Rama.”

Shuka took the form of a bird — and flew through the sky to Sugriva. He delivered Ravana's message — just as Ravana had told him.

But the vanaras saw him. They flew up into the sky towards him — they tried to catch his wings, to strike him. Shuka was afraid — but he finished delivering the message.

Sugriva heard it — and roared —

Sugriva said: “Shuka, listen — Ravana is not my friend, and he never helped me. He is Rama's enemy — so he will be killed, as Vali was killed. I will come to Lanka with my army — and turn it to ash.”

Angada said — “This is not an envoy — this is a spy. Standing in the sky, he is measuring the strength of our whole army. Catch him — do not let him go back to Lanka.”

The vanaras ran to catch Shuka — but Shuka stayed in the sky, and then flew away towards Lanka.

Pause and think — Shuka went as an envoy — but Angada said, this is a spy. What is the difference between an envoy and a spy? And when Sugriva heard Ravana's message, what did he do — was he afraid, or did he roar?

3 · Shuka Returns · · SHUKA RETURNS

Shuka came back to Lanka — and stood before Ravana.

Ravana asked — “Tell me, what did Sugriva say? What are the vanaras doing?”

Shuka said — “Your Majesty, Sugriva did not accept your message. He said — he will come to Lanka with Rama. And the vanaras ran to catch me — I barely saved my life.”

Ravana heard this — and his anger grew. But a fear also settled in his heart — Sugriva had not been afraid.

Ravana thought — talking to Sugriva is useless. Now the army must be known from within.

Meanwhile Rama had crossed the sea — and his army had landed on the far shore.

Pause and think — Shuka told Ravana the truth — that Sugriva was not afraid. Should a spy tell the truth — even when the king will not like it? And when Ravana heard the truth, what did he do — think, or grow angry?

4 · Spies in Vanara Guise · · SPIES IN VANARA GUISE

Rama had crossed the sea with his army and landed. Ravana called his two ministers — Shuka and Sarana — and said —

Ravana said: “Both of you, take the form of vanaras — and enter their army. Count them, learn their strength — who the great vanaras are, what Rama and Lakshmana are doing, and how the bridge was built — learn it all and return.”

Shuka and Sarana took the form of vanaras — and entered the army. The army was so great it could not be counted — on the mountains, in the caves, on the shore of the sea, in the forests — there were vanaras everywhere.

But Vibhishana saw them. He was with Rama — and he knew Ravana's ministers. He caught them both — and brought them before Rama.

Vibhishana said — “Rama, these are Ravana's ministers — Shuka and Sarana. They have come from Lanka as spies.”

The vanaras ran to kill them — but Rama raised his hand and said — (in a calm, steady voice) “Stop.”

Rama said — “A captured messenger who holds no weapon in his hands does not deserve to be killed. Set them free.”

And Rama said to them — “Go to Lanka and tell Ravana — at dawn tomorrow you will see how my arrows have broken Lanka's ramparts and arches.”

Shuka and Sarana bowed to Rama — they praised his sense of dharma — and went back to Lanka.

Pause and think — Why did Rama set the captured spies free? Is sparing an enemy also a kind of strength? And Rama said — one who holds no weapon does not deserve to be killed. Is that rule still right today?

5 · The Two Spies Report · · THE TWO SPIES REPORT

Shuka and Sarana returned to Lanka — and stood before Ravana. Ravana asked — “Tell me — who is in the army?”

Sarana named the great vanaras one by one —

“Your Majesty, there is Sugriva — son of Riksharaja, unconquerable in battle. Jambavan — son of Gadgada, king of the bears. Sushena — son of Yama, valiant and virtuous. Dadhimukha — son of the Moon, cool-minded. Nila — son of Agni, general of the army. Angada — grandson of Indra, young and invincible. Mainda and Dvivida — sons of the Ashvin twins. Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya and Sharabha — all great heroes.”

Shuka too told the count of the army — “Your Majesty, the army is so great it cannot be counted — and all of them are protected by Rama.”

Both of them said — “Your Majesty, Rama alone can defeat Lanka. Return Sita — that is wisdom.”

Ravana heard this — and his face turned red.

Pause and think — Why did Shuka and Sarana tell Ravana the truth — that the army was very great? Were they frightened of Rama — or did they truly wish Ravana well? And when a spy tells the truth, should the king listen?

6 · Ravana Scolds Them · · RAVANA SCOLDS THEM

Ravana scolded Shuka and Sarana — “Both of you praise Rama! You are my ministers, yet you sing of the enemy's power — have you no shame?”

Shuka and Sarana bowed their heads. They said — “Your Majesty, we told you what we saw. We cannot lie.”

Ravana said — “I do not want to hear your words. I will learn for myself how great the army is.”

Ravana called Sardula again — “You go again. This time look even more carefully — who the heroes are, what their strength is — learn it all and return.”

Sardula bowed — and set out again towards the sea.

Pause and think — Why did Ravana scold his own spies? Did he not want to hear the truth — or did he not want to believe it? And when someone scolds the truth-teller, will the next spy still tell the truth?

7 · Sardula Goes Again · · SARDULA GOES AGAIN

Sardula entered the army again — quietly, in hiding. But this time the vanaras were ready. They recognised him — and caught him.

The vanaras pushed him about and paraded him through the whole army — and then brought him before Rama. Sardula trembled — he thought he would now be killed.

But Rama said — (in a calm voice) “Stay! Stay!” — and the vanaras stopped. Rama set Sardula free — as he had set Shuka and Sarana free.

Sardula returned to Lanka — frightened, tired. Ravana looked at him — and said — “Your face has changed. Did the vanaras catch you?”

Sardula said — “Your Majesty, those vanaras cannot be spied upon — they are strong, bold — and protected by Rama. They cannot be talked to — and on every path, mountain-like vanaras stand guard.”

Then Ravana asked — “Tell me — who are the heroes among them?” And Sardula named them one by one — Sugriva, Jambavan, Sushena, Dadhimukha, Nila, Angada, Mainda-Dvivida, Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sharabha — and at the end he said — “And this is Rama — son of Dasharatha, like a lion — who killed Khara, Dushana and Trishira.”

Sardula said — “Your Majesty, Rama's army is camped on Mount Suvela — and Rama has arranged his army in the shape of Garuda. They are advancing towards Lanka. Now you yourself must decide what is to be done.”

Ravana heard this — and was a little troubled. But he said — “I will see — how great Rama is.”

So ends the story of the spies — all three went, all three were caught, all three were set free by Rama — and all three told the truth.

Pause and think — Why did Rama set Sardula free too — even though he had come a second time? Does kindness have an end? And Sardula said at the end — now you yourself must decide. Is a spy's work only to tell — and the king's to decide?

Bigger Thoughts · · BIGGER THOUGHTS

In this book Ravana sent three spies — Sardula, Shuka and Sarana. All three went, all three were caught — and all three were set free by Rama.

Rama said — one who holds no weapon does not deserve to be killed. And all three spies returned and told the truth — the army is very great, Rama is very great, return Sita. Ravana listened to none of them.

Ask your listeners:

1. Why did Ravana send a spy first — is it necessary to know the enemy before a war?

2. Shuka went as an envoy — but Angada said, this is a spy. What is the difference between an envoy and a spy?

3. Why did Rama set the captured spies free — is sparing an enemy also a kind of strength?

4. Why did Shuka and Sarana tell Ravana the truth — that the army was very great?

5. Why did Ravana scold his own spies — did he not want to hear the truth?

6. Why did Rama set Sardula free too — even though he had come a second time? Does kindness have an end?

7. If you were in Rama's place, what would you do with a captured spy — kill him, or set him free?

Where This Story Comes From · · WHERE THIS STORY COMES FROM

Main Source

The main story of this book is Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda, sargas 20 and 24–30 — Shuka and Sarana, the spies.

The First Spy — Sarga 20

Sardula seeing the army and returning to tell Ravana; Ravana sending Shuka to Sugriva as an envoy — this is sarga 20.

Shuka as Envoy — Sarga 20

Shuka taking the form of a bird and going to Sugriva, delivering Ravana's message; the vanaras trying to catch him; Sugriva's answer; Angada saying — this is not an envoy, this is a spy — this is sarga 20.

Shuka Returns — Sarga 24

Shuka returning to Lanka and telling Ravana how he was received — this is sarga 24.

Spies in Vanara Guise — Sarga 25

After Rama crosses the sea, Ravana sending Shuka and Sarana in vanara form into the army; Vibhishana recognising and catching them; Rama setting them free — “a captured messenger who holds no weapon does not deserve to be killed” — and Rama's message — this is sarga 25.

The Two Spies Report — Sargas 26–28

Sarana naming the great vanaras; Shuka telling the count of the army; both advising the return of Sita — this is sargas 26–28.

Ravana Scolds Them — Sarga 29

Ravana scolding Shuka and Sarana and sending Sardula again — this is sarga 29.

Sardula Goes Again — Sarga 30

Sardula being caught, paraded through the army, brought before Rama; Rama saying “Stay! Stay!” and setting him free; Sardula returning to name the great vanaras and telling of Rama's army camped on Mount Suvela, arranged in the shape of Garuda — this is sarga 30.

What Is Not in This Book

Some later tellings say that one of Sardula's eyes was put out — that is not in Valmiki, so it is not told in this book.

What Happens Next

Rama's army is camped on Mount Suvela — and Lanka lies before it. The next story — Mount Suvela and Sarama — is in the next book of this series.

The End · · THE END

Here ends the story of Shuka and Sarana, the spies — all three went, all three were caught, all three were set free by Rama — and all three told the truth.

And whenever you wonder whether kindness should be shown even to an enemy, remember Rama — who said that one who holds no weapon does not deserve to be killed.

— The End —
